notes: Source: 2026 New York Giants Media Guide (IA item new-york-giants-2026-media-guide, 442 pdf pages; PDF page number = printed page number, e.g. pdf p370 prints '370'). Career top-10 tables are 'GIANTS ALL-TIME TOP 10 / TOP TENS' pdf pp. 367-368; 'GIANTS INDIVIDUAL RECORDS' are pdf pp. 369-377 (rushing pp. 370-371, passing p372, receiving pp. 373-374, interceptions p374, sacks p377). Every digit was read from 200 dpi crops of the page pictures.

Regular season: the guide prints its postseason records separately ('INDIVIDUAL POSTSEASON RECORDS', pdf pp. 436-439, not used); the career totals in Top Tens and Individual Records agree (for example Eli Manning 57,023 passing yards).

through_season 2025: the lists include 2025 entries (Brian Burns 16.5 sacks in 2025, Wan'Dale Robinson 92 receptions in 2025, Russell Wilson 450 yards at Dallas Sept. 14, 2025, Cam Skattebo's Oct. 9, 2025 game, Jaxson Dart 2025 elsewhere in the Individual Records) and the guide is the 2026 edition (2026 transactions are listed).

Individual Records print no rank numbers: ranks follow printed order and tied values share the lowest rank (1,2,3,3,5); tie=true marks every tied row; in 'raw' a parenthesised number such as '(14)' is the value printed on an earlier line of the same tie group. Game rows put the opponent before the date in the printed row; years holds MM/DD/YYYY plus the opponent as printed. Red type in the guide marks players on the current (2026) roster (for example Odell Beckham Jr. with the career span '2014-18, 26', Malik Nabers, Brian Burns).

Career passing yards and career interceptions use the 'Top Tens' tables (printed rank numbers, 10 and 12 rows); every other career list uses the Individual Records box. Individual Records and Top Tens agree on the values they share (checked for passing yards, interceptions, rushing yards, receptions, receiving yards and sacks); years can differ slightly between the two sections (Emlen Tunnell '1948-58' in Individual Records vs '1949-58' in Top Tens, Mathias Kiwanuka '2006-14' vs '2006-13'): each list keeps the years of the section it was copied from.

Top Tens interceptors: the guide prints rank '4.' and '5.' for the two players tied at 35 (Willie Williams, Dick Lynch) and no rank for the last two rows tied at 20 with '10. Corey Webster'; rank/tie here follow the equal values (printed ranks kept for 4 and 5 with tie=true, all three 20s are rank 10, tie=true).

Aggregate lines: the guide prints 'on 17 occasions, most recently by Cam Skattebo' (3 rushing TDs), 'four times, most recently Daniel Jones' (5 TD passes), 'on 23 occasions, most recently by Odell Beckham Jr.' (3 receiving TDs), 'on 18 occasions, most recently by Terry Kinard' (3 interceptions) and '34 times, most recently Dexter Lawrence II' (3.0 sacks). Only the named most-recent game of each is copied, flagged tie=true, the other tied games are not named in the guide, so those lists are not complete tie groups.

Derrick Ward's 215-yard game prints the date cut off ('Dec. 21, 200'); the year 2008 in years comes from the guide's own line '14.33 Derrick Ward, vs. Carolina (15-215) Dec. 21, 2008' (same game, 215 yards). raw keeps the cut-off text.

Sacks: the Individual Records heading is 'SACKS (ONLY SINCE 1982)'; the Top Tens sack table footnotes that Taylor's 9.5 rookie sacks (1981) and George Martin's 50.0 sacks (1975-81) are not counted, so Lawrence Taylor's career is 132.5 here.

Names: 'Odell Beckham, Jr.' (printed with a comma in the career lists) is written 'Odell Beckham Jr.'; 'Phillippi Sparks' is printed with that spelling in the Top Tens table. Y.A. Tittle is printed 'Y.A. Tittle'.
Tackles: no tackles record or leader list exists in this guide for any scope, so those three pairs are 'missing'.
